jurisdictions.name: Boise
notes: The city lists separate building, plumbing, electrical, mechanical and erosion and sediment control permits, and homeowners can apply for several of them through its Permitting and Licensing System.

Boise's residential construction brochure says an erosion and sediment control permit is needed for work over 500 sq. ft. of disturbance and/or excavating over 10 cubic yards, and it names swimming pools as included.
The homeowner's guide says some projects, such as taller retaining walls, need an Idaho-licensed engineer.

sources.title: Homeowner's Guide - City of Boise Planning and Development Services
PDS Residential Construction Brochure 2023 - City of Boise

jurisdictions.name: Meridian
notes: Meridian's handout says prefabricated swimming pools not deeper than 4 feet need no building permit, while all other swimming pools do.
Pools needing a permit cannot encroach into property easements; the handout gives typical easements as 10 ft rear and 5 ft side and says to check the recorded plat.
The handout tells applicants to verify setbacks with Meridian Planning and to check homeowner's association requirements before placing a structure.
Meridian's handout states that any electrical work needs an electrical permit.

sources.title: Residential Detached Accessory Structures - City of Meridian Community Development

jurisdictions.name: Coeur d'Alene
notes: Residential building, plumbing, mechanical and re-roof permits can be applied for through the city's Online Permits Access site, which needs a separate account.
Residential building permit applications need one set of drawings and specifications in PDF format, and the plan review fee is due at submittal.

sources.title: Online Permits Access - City of Coeur d'Alene
Residential Applications - City of Coeur d'Alene Building Services
